public_lecture_sections.lecture_title: Lecture 1: Experimental measurements require a readable signal

modules.module_title: Assay readouts link a biological process to a measurable signal
modules.explanation: An assay is useful only when the measured signal is coupled to the biological process being tested. The readout must change when the process changes, and the control condition must show the baseline signal so that a treatment effect can be separated from background variation.

blocks.content: A high signal is not automatically a biological effect; it may reflect background, saturation, poor normalization, or a reagent-specific artefact.

public_lecture_sections.lecture_title: Lecture 2: Controls define the interpretation boundary

modules.module_title: Negative and positive controls test different parts of the claim
modules.explanation: A negative control estimates the signal expected without the tested process, while a positive control verifies that the assay can detect the process when it is present. Together they define whether a failed result is biologically meaningful or simply an assay failure.

blocks.content: A negative control protects against false positives; a positive control protects against false negatives.
